sum003:
The Grandmother's Unforgettable Journey of Immigration to America

I was a new immigrant in the United States, but I still found myself facing many challenges. As a young girl growing up on a small farm in Poland, life was tough, and my parents worked long hours for little pay. My family needed every penny we could earn. And so, when my parents decided to immigrate to America in 1923, they packed all our belongings into a trunk and set out on what felt like the most perilous journey of their lives.

It took us three years to reach the United States. We landed in San Francisco and made our way to New York City by train. There were many hardships along the way, as we traveled through Mexico and Central America, and we finally arrived in Texas. For me, one of the most challenging experiences was when my parents first crossed the border into the United States. They were stopped at a checkpoint by U.S. Customs, and they were forced to lie down for over an hour while officers searched their belongings. It was the longest day of our lives, but we finally got through and made it to the other side.

After our arrival in America, we struggled to find work and support ourselves. I worked odd jobs as a housekeeper, gardener, and babysitter, but it wasn't enough to provide for my family. We lived in poverty, and food was scarce. It was hard to make ends meet, but I never stopped trying. I learned how to read and write, how to sew, and how to garden. And with each new experience, I became more resilient and determined to find a better life for myself and my family.

Today, I am proud of everything I've achieved as an immigrant. I have a loving husband and two amazing children, who make me proud every day. And even though there are still challenges on the road ahead, I know that with hard work and determination, we can succeed in life.
